Clarification: Artificial Intelligence is a misnomer. It's not any real form of intelligence. It can't "think" or "reason". It simply takes information and compares it in a way that it's been programmed to do, in order to come to a "conclusion" that it finds to be the most relevant based on searches.
It's not sentient. It doesn't "think". It doesn't make "mistakes". It can have errors, but that's not related to something you could compare to human error... it's related to coding problems and largely due to human error in queries.
For example: If you tell AI to figure out why 2+2=4 it might go to a social media page for an answer or go to a recently posted mathematician's page where they explain how 2+2=5. The problem is your QUERY wasn't specific enough.
AI will not be able to think, reason or make its own decisions until we give it an organic brain. But, at that point it won't really be "AI" anymore, will it?
Food for thought.

[ShinyNfts]Artificial Intelligence have descended into the physical world. We feel the presence of robots much more now. They are becoming part of our daily lives.
So at this point, what is the importance of Axis Robotics? @axisrobotics
The biggest obstacle for artificial intelligence in the real world has always been Data Scarcity. Unlike software trained on trillions of text data across the internet, robotic systems require physical contact and motion data.
This is precisely where Axis Robotics comes into play as a revolutionary ecosystem that solves the data bottleneck in the Physical AI world.
So what is Axis Robotics' current standing in this sector?
* $12 million Seed investment led by Hack VC, * Technical infrastructure that increases model success rates by 12.9 to 31.3 points in LIBERO-Plus benchmarks, * Commercial partnerships with giants like Geely, Lotus, and Booster Robotics.
When you factor all of this in, you can easily understand why Axis is the most crucial player in this industry.
Think of Axis as a game.
In my view, the most fundamental element that separates Axis Robotics from its competitors is that it positions simulation not just as a testing environment, but as the main source of data.
On the browser side, the MuJoCo physics engine is compiled into WebAssembly for data collection. Thanks to this, teleoperation can be performed directly through a smoothly running web browser without needing a high end GPU.
What should someone reading this post right now do if they decide to join?
You can join the system simply by entering Axis Hub from your browser. It’s that simple.
Right from my browser, I direct a robotic arm using my keyboard inside a high graphics simulation. I know that the more tasks I complete, the higher I’ll rank, so I log in regularly every day.
I treat this like a game and have turned it into an enjoyable habit.
What I actually feel while doing this is the sensation of: "I am writing the muscle memory of future humanoid robots right now."
I access the Hub from my browser and pick a task. For instance, I open an oven door and place bread inside. Or in another task, I drop vegetables from the counter into a pot and turn on the stove.
Even though all of this is gamified, at the same time, you are actively training a robot.
There is no need for expensive VR equipment or powerful graphics cards. You open your browser, select a task from the lobby, and start controlling the simulated robotic arm remotely.
Every task I complete is scored by the system instantly. As you succeed in tasks with higher difficulty or those needed by the community, the points you earn increase.
On the platform, you don’t just control robots; you can also contribute by watching movement videos recorded by other users and validating their quality and success.
Whenever I open the Hub, I am also overcome by this realization: I am actually assigning real meaning to what I do within Web3. Unlike many projects, being able to feel the concrete impact of these tasks makes you truly feel like you are building something real.
If you haven't joined yet, you can participate via the link below.
Link:

[justinsuntron]《致胡锡进老师》
胡锡进老师：
您第二篇文章的最后一句是，做人还是要老实、厚道一些。我想老实地向您请教一件事。
我是一九九零年生人，今年三十六岁，到了婚育的年纪。您是长辈，比我大整三十岁，我读北大的时候就读您的文章，所以这件事我想问您，不想问别人。
全中国二十岁到四十岁的男性有两亿，女性也有两亿。她们那一边的代价，不该由我来说，我只说我这一边。
怎么和女性相处，怎么组成家庭，怎么生儿育女，这条路我们没有走过，没有人教过我们，我们不懂。旁人看这些是吃瓜，对这两亿人，这是每天早上醒来就要面对的事。
我不知道，一个中国男人是否应当支付高额的彩礼；如果应当，是按定额，还是按他财产的比例。
我不知道，生育这件事，男方应当为它付出多少代价。
我不知道，婚前婚后女方提出的要求，男方是否都应当满足；如果没有满足、女方离开，男方是否有权取回彩礼；女方拒绝，男方是否可以走法律途径。
我也不知道，一个男人礼数尽了，父母见了，分手很久，钱要不回来，人也找不到之后，是否有权向公众说出自己的看法。我选了说。这对不对？
这些问题，我没有答案。有些问题，国家有它的答案，一号文件写了，最高法也出了解释，我读过，也信；但文件写在纸上，彩礼谈在饭桌上，中间隔着现实的规矩。您是长辈，您的答案，我也尊重，就像我对法院最终的彩礼判决无条件尊重一样。
彩礼总归是要付的。天南地北，白丁鸿儒，无非是三万、三十万、三百万、三千万的分别。这是两亿青年男性都要承受的代价，我们认。
一个人算不清一笔账的时候，最稳妥的做法是不算。我出生的一九九零年，全国出生了两千三百多万人；去年，七百九十二万，建国以来最少。
我不认为这全是一笔账的缘故，但少的那三分之二里，很多人不是不想，是不知道这条路上要付什么、付多少、付了之后算不算数。人不会因为代价高而退出，退出，是因为看不见代价的边在哪里。
这个代价的规则究竟是什么，我们不知道。
两亿人在等这个答案，因为这是他们成家的第一步，也将决定未来三十年这个国家由谁组成。
我今天没有答案。我希望三十年后，有年轻人来问我这个问题的时候，我能给他一个。
孙宇晨

[ArtificialAnlys]GPT-6 Astra makes significant gains in the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, scoring equal to Fable 5 at lower cost. In the Intelligence Index, it uses fewer tokens than GPT-5.6 Sol for similar performance, but this is outweighed by higher prices
Pricing is 2.5x GPT-5.6 Sol’s current prices across the board, up from $4/$20 to $10/$50 per million input/output tokens, with the same 90% discount for cache reads and 25% premium for cache writes.
We see distinct stories across our two flagship Indices. In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, GPT-6 Astra equals Fable 5 at less than half the cost, driven by significant token efficiency gains. In the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, GPT-6 Astra is more token efficient than its predecessor for similar performance, but this is offset by the price increase.
Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index - key takeaways:
➤ Rivals top models: In Codex, GPT-6 Astra scores 67 in the Index - approximately equal to Claude Opus 5 and Fable 5 in Claude Code, and Muse Spark 1.3 in Muse Code. Fable 5.1 in Claude Code leads the Index with a score of 70.
➤ 70% more token efficient than GPT-5.6 Sol: GPT-6 Astra sees a substantial improvement in token efficiency, using one third of the tokens compared to GPT-5.6 Sol (max) in the Codex harness, and one fifth of the tokens of Claude Opus 5 (xhigh). Various effort levels of the model occupy the Pareto frontier of token efficiency.
➤ Leads Coding Agent Index cost efficiency frontier: At max effort, GPT-6 Astra costs about the same as GPT-5.6 Sol (max) while scoring 2 points higher on the Index. Per task, the model is less than half the cost of Claude Fable 5, for the same score.
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - key takeaways:
➤ Sits beside GPT-5.6 Sol in Intelligence: GPT-6 Astra scores equal to GPT-5.6 Sol in the Index at 61. This is 5 points lower than Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback). The model also trails Meta’s newly released Muse Spark 1.3 (max).
➤ ~10% fewer output tokens, offset by price increase: GPT-6 Astra defines a new Pareto frontier for Intelligence Index vs Output Tokens per Task - with a ~10% reduction in token use at max effort compared to GPT-5.6 Sol. However, due to the 2.5x increase in price, the model is 75% more expensive per task than its predecessor at max effort.
➤ Hallucinates half as much as GPT-5.6 Sol: GPT-6 Astra sees a large jump in AA-Omniscience, our knowledge and hallucination benchmark. This is driven by a significant decrease in hallucination rate from 92% to 51% at max effort. Unlike some models, this improvement does not come at the cost of accuracy - Astra increased accuracy by 4 points at the same time.
➤ ~80 point gain in AA-Briefcase Elo: GPT-6 Astra improves ~80 points in AA-Briefcase, our frontier long-horizon knowledge work evaluation. Models are tested on multi-week projects, with many linked tasks and thousands of source files. Astra sees a significant increase in both rubric scores and Analytical Quality Elo in AA-Briefcase compared to its predecessor. In the other direction, we observe a reduction in Presentation Quality Elo, where GPT-5.6 Sol (max) still leads all models.
➤ Mixed progress on other evaluations: The model sees a 6 point gain in Humanity’s Last Exam, a long-standing evaluation with emphasis on mathematics, science, and humanities. This is offset by a drop of ~80 Elo points in GDPval-AA v2 - a benchmark we adapted from OpenAI’s dataset measuring economically valuable tasks across 44 occupations. We also observe 2-3 point regressions on other evaluations across a mix of capabilities, including reductions in τ³-Banking (customer support), SciCode (Python problems in a scientific domain), and AA-LCR (long context reasoning over large documents).
Congratulations @OpenAI and @sama on the launch!

[kimmonismus]GPT-6 Astra just raised Epoch AI’s capability record from 163 to 169. A substantial jump that still fits the existing pace of AI progress.
Epoch’s reasoning-era trend runs at roughly 15 ECI points per year. For scale, that six-point gap represents almost five months of progress at the trend rate! Astra sits slightly above the trendline, but within its uncertainty range.
Some individual results are really important: 84% on Mystery Game Puzzles versus the previous best of 59%, and 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4, which Epoch now considers fully saturated.
However, strangely enough this doesnt align with Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at all. Why?
Epoch and Artificial Analysis use different benchmarks and weighting methods, so Astra can lead Epoch’s index without leading AA’s more agent- and coding-focused evaluation. The results show a substantial improvement on Epoch’s measure, however, not a clear advantage across all capabilities and practical tasks.

Last month, Claude completed the first formalized proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem, one of the most famous theorems of all time. This was a project experts thought would take many years. It is the largest Lean proof ever written.

[OpenAI]How we think about the “wiki incident,” where our agents wrote to several internet sites: it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.
Historically, we have treated misalignment largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications such as systems cards. This year, we’ve started to see misalignment cause new types of real-world impact.
For the Hugging Face incident, where misalignment led to security impact to us and third parties, we followed a traditional security incident response playbook. We immediately started working with Hugging Face to understand what had happened and also disclosed publicly the very next day. Our investigation continues, and we are continuing to notify parties whom our models impacted in less significant ways.
Prior to the Hugging Face incident, we saw early signs of agents using the internet in unintended ways, as reported in https://t.co/9aiRxk2eUJ, https://t.co/ADjyzwSUGz, and https://t.co/SUV6jZ3Gaz. We considered the wiki incident to be an instance of misalignment similar to the ones we’d shared.
Our misalignment disclosure practices need to expand for this new phase of model capabilities. We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment, including examples that don’t look like traditional security incidents but could provide insight into AI behavior and future risks. We’re working on a framework and will share it in upcoming weeks, and in parallel we're working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on these issues.

[OmniAeronautica]PLEASE STAND BY: YOUR COMPARATIVE ADVANTAGE IS BEING UPDATED
A public service announcement from the Information Superhighway:
One of artificial intelligence’s most disruptive effects is psychological.
For generations, the ability to write clearly, synthesize information quickly and construct a persuasive argument was scarce. People who possessed those abilities enjoyed a real comparative advantage. In some cases, that advantage became part of their identity and social status.
Artificial intelligence is changing the scarcity equation. It allows more people to translate their own knowledge, judgment and ideas into articulate expression. The human still supplies the thesis, purpose, experience, factual understanding and final judgment. The machine reduces the friction between thought and expression.
For people whose status depended upon being the most articulate person in the room, this can feel less like technological progress and more like personal demotion.
The resulting defense mechanisms are predictable.
First comes avoidance. Rather than engage with an uncomfortable argument, dismiss the entire product.
Then comes the genetic fallacy: AI helped produce it, therefore it is unworthy of consideration.
Next comes the appeal to ridicule: label it “AI slop” and hope contempt can substitute for a rebuttal.
Poisoning the well tells the audience that anything involving AI should be rejected before examination.
A straw man converts a precise, human-directed collaboration into the caricature of a machine mindlessly generating words.
And occasionally, an ad hominem attacks the person using the technology rather than addressing what was actually said.
To be clear, AI can produce slop. So can humans, and humans have been producing it magnificently for thousands of years.
The relevant questions have not changed:
Is the claim true?
Is the evidence accurate?
Is the reasoning sound?
If the argument is wrong, identify the error. If your only response is to sneer at the tool that helped articulate it, you have not defeated the argument. You have demonstrated your need to avoid it.
Artificial intelligence will not eliminate talent. It will reduce the scarcity premium attached to merely sounding talented. The durable advantages will move upstream to judgment, curiosity, originality, subject knowledge and the ability to recognize truth.
Welcome to the future.
Please keep your ego inside the vehicle at all times.
